"'''Hey, Soul Sister'''" is a song by American [[rock music|rock]] band [[Train (band)|Train]]. It was written by lead singer [[Pat Monahan]], [[Amund Bjørklund]], and [[Espen Lind]]. It was released as the lead single from the band's fifth studio album, ''[[Save Me, San Francisco]]'' (2009).

The song reached number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart and is Train's highest-charting song to date. It was the top-selling song on the [[iTunes Store]] in 2010,<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hey-soul-sister-is-top-itunes-song-of-2010/ | publisher=CBS News | title="Hey, Soul Sister" Is Top iTunes Song of 2010 | date=December 9, 2010}}</ref> and the second overall best-selling song in the US in 2010.<ref name="What Santa Brought">[http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/72698/week-ending-dec-26-2009-what-santa-brought/ What Santa Brought] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102021435/http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/72698/week-ending-dec-26-2009-what-santa-brought |date=January 2, 2011}} by Paul Grein in Chart Watch</ref> It is also the band's most commercially successful single to date, reaching number one in 16 countries. The single received a [[RIAA certification|11× platinum]] [[Music recording certification|certification]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) on October 5, 2022, signifying sales of over eleven million copies.<ref name="RIAA"/> It was also certified 15× Platinum in Australia and Diamond in Canada. The live iTunes version of "Hey, Soul Sister" garnered a [[Grammy Award]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals]] at the [[53rd Annual Grammy Awards]]. The song was not eligible for any Grammy Award in the [[List of Grammy Award categories#General Field|General Field]].

"Hey, Soul Sister" is a song by American rock band Train. It was written by lead singer Pat Monahan, Amund Bjørklund, and Espen Lind. It was released as the lead single from the band's fifth studio album, Save Me, San Francisco (2009).

The song reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and is Train's highest-charting song to date. It was the top-selling song on the iTunes Store in 2010, and the second overall best-selling song in the US in 2010. It is also the band's most commercially successful single to date, reaching number one in 16 countries. The single received a 11× platinum certification by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) on October 5, 2022, signifying sales of over eleven million copies. It was also certified 15× Platinum in Australia and Diamond in Canada. The live iTunes version of "Hey, Soul Sister" garnered a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals at the 53rd Annual Grammy Awards. The song was not eligible for any Grammy Award in the General Field.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: After collaborating with the Norwegian production duo Espionage (Espen Lind and Amund Bjørklund) in the writing and recording of the track "Brick by Brick", Train's lead singer Pat Monahan decided to record another track with the duo. He initially wanted to write a song in the style of [[INXS]], and requested that the Norwegian duo play that type of song; from their performance, he wrote the lyrics and melodies for a song that was eventually titled "Hey, Soul Sister". However, he was not satisfied until Lind recommended a ukulele, which, in Monahan's mind, "made my words dance". Lead guitarist Jimmy Stafford had to learn to play the ukulele with lessons on the internet, having to adapt to a "flamenco style" of playing as opposed to the pick-heavy method of a normal guitar.<ref name="GoErie">[http://www.goerie.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20091107/NEWS02/311079974/-1/RSS01 "Train adds ukulele to make 'Hey, Soul Sister' a chart topper"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110218163049/http://www.goerie.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20091107/NEWS02/311079974/-1/RSS01 |date=February 18, 2011 }} by Dave Richards, posted November 7, 2009</ref> The lyrics came about from Monahan imagining what the [[Burning Man]], which he never went, must be like, envisioning attractive women dancing around the huge wooden man.<ref name="You Sing, I Write">[https://yousingiwrite.blogspot.com/2009/10/q-with-train.html "Q&A with Train."] by Annie Reuter, posted October 28, 2009</ref><ref name="105.1 The Buzz">[http://blogs.1051thebuzz.com/category/sheryl-stewart/artist-interviews/ "Train Visits The Buzz Studios!"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100731012901/http://blogs.1051thebuzz.com/category/sheryl-stewart/artist-interviews/ |date=July 31, 2010}} by Sheryl Stewart, posted December 22, 2009</ref><ref name="Hot 104.7">[http://www.hot1047.com/music/hot-music-news/14429-train-frontman-tells-story-behind-hey-soul-sister.html "Train frontman tells story behind 'Hey, Soul Sister'"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101225115240/http://www.hot1047.com/music/hot-music-news/14429-train-frontman-tells-story-behind-hey-soul-sister.html |date=December 25, 2010}}, posted August 23, 2010</ref>

He initially wanted to write a song in the style of INXS, and requested that the Norwegian duo play that type of song; from their performance, he wrote the lyrics and melodies for a song that was eventually titled "Hey, Soul Sister". However, he was not satisfied until Lind recommended a ukulele, which, in Monahan's mind, "made my words dance". Lead guitarist Jimmy Stafford had to learn to play the ukulele with lessons on the internet, having to adapt to a "flamenco style" of playing as opposed to the pick-heavy method of a normal guitar. The lyrics came about from Monahan imagining what the Burning Man, which he never went, must be like, envisioning attractive women dancing around the huge wooden man.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: For the song, the band returned to their [[folk rock]] roots emphasizing, "super catchy riffs and melodies" over production gimmicks.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/267800/train-song-debut-hey-soul-sister|title=Train Song Debut: "Hey Soul Sister"|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> The song is characterized by a signature pattern played by [[Espen Lind]] on a ukulele.<ref name="GoErie"/> Its chorus references the band [[Mr. Mister]].

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
"Hey, Soul Sister" received mixed reviews from critics.

''[[The Village Voice]]'' derided the song, quipping "'Hey Soul Sister' is an orgy where bad ideas trade STDs, and the most syphilitic brain-fart stumbled in drunk from a [[Smash Mouth]] show ... From Smash Mouth, Train picked up an earworm that burrowed into society's asshole, laid 4.7 million iTunes eggs, and gave birth to a grey cloud of banality that covers the Earth."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.villagevoice.com/2010/12/22/the-20-worst-songs-of-2010-1-train-hey-soul-sister/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715093518/https://www.villagevoice.com/2010/12/22/the-20-worst-songs-of-2010-1-train-hey-soul-sister/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2018|title=The 20 Worst Songs of 2010, #1: Train, "Hey, Soul Sister"|date=December 22, 2010|website=The Village Voice}}</ref> ''[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]]'' concurred with the ''Village Voice'', approvingly quoting from the ''Village Voice'''s review that "there is less soul in the entirety of Train than in the palest single member of [[Collective Soul]]. 'Hey, Soul Sister' is soul for people who refer to peanut butter and jelly as 'soul food.' It makes [[the California Raisins]] look like the second coming of [[Sly and the Family Stone]]. It's so white, [[Sarah Palin]] just named it her running mate for 2012."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2010/12/worst-song-year/|title=Is This The Worst Song Of the Year?|first=Tim|last=Murphy|work=Mother Jones}}</ref>

In a tamer review, ''[[Business Insider]]'' named "Hey, Soul Sister" the worst song of 2010 describing it as a "saccharine, falsettoed ear-bleeder."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/worst-top-10-hit-song-every-year-since-2000-2018-7 |title=The worst hit song of every year since 2000, from Macklemore to Train (twice) |first=John |last=Lynch |website=Business Insider}}</ref> ''[[LA Weekly]]'' took aim at [[Pat Monahan]]'s lyrical content, awarding "Hey, Soul Sister" places two through ten in its Top 10 worst lyrics of 2010 list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laweekly.com/top-10-worst-lyrics-of-2010/ |title=Top 10 Worst Lyrics of 2010 |date=December 23, 2010 |website=LA Weekly}}</ref>

Alternatively, Scott Mervis, writing for the ''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'', praised the song as a welcome comeback from the band's hiatus, calling the track "joyous" and "bouncy".<ref>{{cite web |date=March 25, 2010 |title=Train stages an unlikely comeback with the bouncy hit 'Hey, Soul Sister' |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/ae/music/2010/03/25/Train-stages-an-unlikely-comeback-with-the-bouncy-hit-Hey-Soul-Sister/stories/201003250291 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref>

It has also been featured in several TV shows: ''[[CSI: NY]]'' in the episode "Second Chances", ''[[Hellcats]]'' in its first episode, and ''[[Medium (TV series)|Medium]]'' in chapter [[List of Medium episodes#Season 6 (2009–2010)|6x03]] "[[List of Medium episodes (season 6)#Episode list|Pain Killer]]". It has also been played in the Canadian TV show ''[[Being Erica]]'', in chapter 3x11. The song was performed on ABC's ''[[Dancing with the Stars (US TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]]'' on May 4, 2010, and on ''America's Got Talent'' on July 21, 2010. The [[Dixie Chicks]] covered this song while on their 2010 tour with [[The Eagles]].

In [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]]'s TV musical-comedy series ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'' the song was covered in the ninth episode of [[Glee (season 2)|season two]], "[[Special Education (Glee)|Special Education]]" (aired November 30, 2010), by actor [[Darren Criss]] (as his character [[Blaine Anderson]]) singing the solo in a performance with the fictional show choir [[Dalton Academy Warblers]] (voiced by all-male [[a cappella]] group [[Beelzebubs]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2010/11/24/glee-darren-criss-train-hey-soul-sister,|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929131838/http://insidetv.ew.com/2010/11/24/glee-darren-criss-train-hey-soul-sister,/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 29, 2012|title=TV|work=Entertainment Weekly's EW.com}}</ref>

Also in [[Australia]], it was performed by Robbie Anderson on [[The Voice Kids (Australian TV series)|''The Voice Kids'']]. The song was performed by [[Street Corner Symphony (group)|Street Corner Symphony]] on the second season of the television show ''[[The Sing-Off]]'' during [[The Sing-Off (season 2)#Episode 2 (December 8, 2010)|episode 2: "Songs From The Past 5 Years"]].  In 2010, the dance troupe from ''[[Strictly Come Dancing]]'' performed a quickstep to the song and it was used in a [[Samsung]] 3D TV commercial.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J2Gr7q2HzM8 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211220/J2Gr7q2HzM8 |archive-date=2021-12-20 |url-status=live|title=Samsung 3D LED TV "Aquarium" :60TV|via=YouTube|date=February 22, 2017|access-date=March 15, 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref> It was also used by Spanish telecommunications company [[Movistar]] in commercials from their Latin America operations in 2010.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"Hey, Soul Sister" debuted at #98 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for the week ended October 17, 2009, becoming their first charting single in five years. On the week of January 30, 2010, in its 16th week on the Hot 100 chart, "Hey, Soul Sister" leaped to #7 from #23 on an 81% digital single sales increase from the previous week, thus becoming Train's second career Top Ten hit on the chart. It reached #3 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 in the week of April 10, 2010, and it is their highest on the chart to date, even surpassing their 2001 hit, "[[Drops of Jupiter (Tell Me)|Drops of Jupiter]]", which peaked at #5. The song climbed to #1 on the [[Hot Digital Songs]] chart for the week of April 10, 2010, and stayed in the top spot for three weeks. As of the January 20, 2011, issue of ''Billboard'', "Hey, Soul Sister" had spent 22 weeks at number one on the [[Adult Contemporary]] chart.

The single sold 687,000 copies in 2009 which made it that year's #131 song. It went on to sell 3,319,000 more units in the first half of 2010 and 42 weeks after its release still stood at number 16 on the Hot 100 chart. By the end of December 2010, it had sold 4,310,000 digital copies, becoming the second biggest selling digital song of that year.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/473767/eminems-recovery-is-2010s-best-selling-album-katy-perrys-california-gurls-top|title=Eminem's 'Recovery' Is 2010's Best-Selling Album; Katy Perry's 'California Gurls' Top Digital Song|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> By the end of January 2011, it had sold over 5 million digital copies.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/The-Nielsen-Company-bw-2049624764.html?x=0 |title=The Nielsen Company & Billboard's 2010 Music Industry Report |publisher=Nielsen SoundScan |via=Yahoo! Finance |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110113080552/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/The-Nielsen-Company-bw-2049624764.html?x=0 |archive-date=January 13, 2011}}</ref> As of January 2014, the song had sold 6,417,000 digital units in the United States, one of the biggest-selling digital singles by a rock band since [[Nielsen SoundScan]] began tracking download sales in 2003.<ref name="yahoo_2013">{{cite news |url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/music-news/chart-watch-radioactive-sets-rock-record-001439867.html |title=Can You Believe "Don't Stop Believin'" Loses Spot as Best-Selling Rock Song? |first=Paul |last=Grein |work=Chart Watch |publisher=Yahoo |date=January 2, 2014}}</ref>

[[BNA Records]], a [[country music]] label owned by Sony Music, released the song to the country music format in June 2010. It debuted at #60 on the [[Hot Country Songs]] charts for the week ended July 10, 2010.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/chart-beat-wednesday-train-dirty-heads-nicki-minaj/|title=Chart Beat Wednesday: Train, Dirty Heads, Nicki Minaj|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=June 30, 2010|magazine=Billboard|access-date=July 1, 2010}}</ref>

In addition to revitalizing Train's career in their native country, "Hey, Soul Sister" topped the [[ARIA Singles Chart]] for four weeks,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Train&titel=Hey%2C+Soul+Sister&cat=s |title=Train – Hey, Soul Sister |publisher=australian-charts.com |access-date=August 9, 2010}}</ref> the [[Dutch Top 40]] for seven,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.top40.nl/train/train-hey-soul-sister-20958|title=Train - Hey, Soul Sister|language=nl|publisher=[[Dutch Top 40]]|access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref> and the [[Irish Singles Chart]]. "Hey, Soul Sister" debuted at #98 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week ended October 17, 2009, becoming their first charting single in five years. On the week of January 30, 2010, in its 16th week on the Hot 100 chart, "Hey, Soul Sister" leaped to #7 from #23 on an 81% digital single sales increase from the previous week, thus becoming Train's second career Top Ten hit on the chart. It reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the week of April 10, 2010, and it is their highest on the chart to date, even surpassing their 2001 hit, "Drops of Jupiter", which peaked at #5. The song climbed to #1 on the Hot Digital Songs chart for the week of April 10, 2010, and stayed in the top spot for three weeks. As of the January 20, 2011, issue of Billboard, "Hey, Soul Sister" had spent 22 weeks at number one on the Adult Contemporary chart.

The single sold 687,000 copies in 2009 which made it that year's #131 song. It went on to sell 3,319,000 more units in the first half of 2010 and 42 weeks after its release still stood at number 16 on the Hot 100 chart. By the end of December 2010, it had sold 4,310,000 digital copies, becoming the second biggest selling digital song of that year. By the end of January 2011, it had sold over 5 million digital copies. As of January 2014, the song had sold 6,417,000 digital units in the United States, one of the biggest-selling digital singles by a rock band since Nielsen SoundScan began tracking download sales in 2003.

BNA Records, a country music label owned by Sony Music, released the song to the country music format in June 2010. It debuted at #60 on the Hot Country Songs charts for the week ended July 10, 2010.

In addition to revitalizing Train's career in their native country, "Hey, Soul Sister" topped the ARIA Singles Chart for four weeks, the Dutch Top 40 for seven, and the Irish Singles Chart. The song was the best performer on the Dutch Top 40 of 2010. In Italy and New Zealand, "Hey, Soul Sister" was blocked from number one by songs recorded by artists native to each country: "Un colpo all'anima" by Ligabue in the former, and "You Got Me" by J. Williams in the latter.

The song spent 21 weeks in the top 40 and only one in the top-20, its peak position of number 18. In Canada, the song was the sixth-best-selling of 2010 with 244,000 copies.
